problem_type: canvas batch model picker execution-mode ambiguity
symptom: After a dependency edge split one image batch into text-to-image and reference-image-edit groups, both model pickers were rendered as '图片 ×1', so users and the Electron acceptance journey could not tell which nodes each picker would change.
direct_cause: CanvasBulkModelSelect built its visible and accessible label from executionKind and count only, even though grouping and model-option filtering had already become requiredMode-aware.
class_root: The shared batch-picker presentation contract did not require every independently actionable execution group to have a distinct user-facing label.
affected_population: Canvas users batch-selecting same-kind nodes that require different generation modes
Image, video, audio, and 3D batch groups whose available model lists differ by requiredMode
Both the selection toolbar and the no-selection batch generation dock
entry_points: Any future CanvasBulkModelSelect caller with multiple required modes for one execution kind
internal_only_reason: This is an internal Nomi grouping and accessible-label invariant; third-party documentation cannot decide how separate canvas execution groups must be named.
invariants: Every simultaneously rendered CanvasBulkModelSelect action has a label that uniquely identifies its affected execution group.
A single-mode execution kind retains the compact kind-and-count label.
When one execution kind is split across required modes, both visible and accessible labels include the localized required mode.

recurrence.reason: The batch grouper can split every billing kind by requiredMode, and any caller that labels only by executionKind can recreate indistinguishable actions.
same_class_scan: Searched all CanvasBulkModelSelect call sites and found two independently rendered entry points: CanvasSelectionToolbar and CanvasBatchGenerateDock.
Inspected groupGenerationNodesByExecutionKind and its tests; image and video already split into text/reference modes, while audio and 3D share the same generic grouping mechanism.
Inspected the shared model-selection structure gate and confirmed both canvas entry points intentionally converge on CanvasBulkModelSelect, making it the earliest common presentation boundary.

generality_proof: Both existing batch-picker entry points pass their complete peer-group set into CanvasBulkModelSelect, whose label-key resolver disambiguates any same-kind, different-mode group before the shared NomiSelect receives either its visible or aria label.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Choose the compact kind label for single-mode groups and a required-mode label whenever peer actions of the same kind would otherwise be indistinguishable.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The selection toolbar passes its complete executionGroups collection to every shared CanvasBulkModelSelect instance.
The bottom dock passes its complete executionGroups collection to the same shared CanvasBulkModelSelect boundary.

prevention.invariant: Same-kind peer actions with different requiredMode values cannot receive the same label key.
prevention.failure_mode: Callers that omit the peer-group context fail TypeScript validation, and same-kind groups with different requiredMode values always resolve to different mode-qualified label keys.
prevention.strategy: Resolve label identity once in the shared picker and require every caller to supply the peer set used to detect ambiguity.

legacy_paths.rationale: There is already one shared picker implementation; the repair changes its labeling contract rather than replacing a parallel legacy path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The defect is owned by Nomi's execution grouping and localization logic and does not depend on a third-party package version.

migration: No persisted project or catalog data changes. Existing groups are relabeled from current runtime state when the toolbar or dock renders.
residual_risks: A future batch picker outside CanvasBulkModelSelect could bypass this contract; the source-structure test currently covers all repository canvas call sites.
